name: Question 6
problem:
Express $z=\frac{4}{1+\text{i}\sqrt{3}}$ in the form $r(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ).$ Give the **exact** values of $r$ and $\theta ,$ in **radians** from $[0,2\pi ).$

$z=$
{{field-1}}$\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡(${{field-2}}$)+i\operatorname{sin}⁡(${{field-3}}$))$
worked_solution:
First, we express the given complex number in the form $z=x+y\text{i}.$ To do this, we remove $\text{i}$ from the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator of $z$ by the complex conjugate of the denominator, which is $1-\text{i}\sqrt{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{4}{1+\text{i}\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{4(1-\text{i}\sqrt{3})}{(1+\text{i}\sqrt{3})(1-\text{i}\sqrt{3})} \\  & =\frac{4-4\text{i}\sqrt{3}}{{1}^{2}-{(\text{i}\sqrt{3})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4-4\text{i}\sqrt{3}}{1-(-3)} \\  & =\frac{4-4i\sqrt{3}}{4} \\  & =1-\sqrt{3}\,i\end{aligned}
$$

In polar form, $r$ represents the magnitude $|z|.$ For a complex number $z=x+y\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.
$$

So, for $z=1-\sqrt{3}\,i,$ the magnitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{(\sqrt{3})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+3} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar form, $\theta $  represents the argument $\operatorname{arg}⁡(z).$ Since $x=1$ and $y=-\sqrt{3},$ $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant. So, we can find $\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\sqrt{3}) \\  & =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the complex number $z$ in polar form:

$$
z=2\cdot \,(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3}))
$$

In polar form, r represents the magnitude |z|. For a complex number z=x+yi, the magnitude of z is given by |z|=x2+y2.

So, for z=1−3i, the magnitude is r=|z|=12+(3)2=1+3=4=2.

In polar form, θ represents the argument arg⁡(z). Since x=1 and y=−3, z lies in the fourth quadrant. So, we can find θ as follows: θ=arg⁡(z)=arctan⁡(yx)=arctan⁡(−3)=2π−π3=5π3

Finally, we write the complex number z in polar form: z=2⋅(cos⁡(5π3)+isin⁡(5π3))
